In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of the phase shifter operation criteria for the azimuthally magnetized waveguide, and with the analysis of the structure characteristics of this type of phase shifter.
the analysis of the phase shifter characteristics in a frequency interval, where the structure operates as a digital non-reciprocal phase shifer.
the analysis of phase characteristics of a coaxial waveguide filled with azimuthally ferrite magnetized to the extent that it is capable of operating as a nonreciprocal digital phase shifter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for the coaxial structure, filled with azimuthally ferrite, to operate as a phase shifter, the following conditions should be fulfilled: 1) the off-diagonal permeability tensor element must be positive, 2) the normalized frequency must be greater than the cut-off frequency and 3) the normalized frequency should not exceed a value, which is less than the cut-off one by a certain quantity.

a coaxial ferrite-filled waveguide can be used as a phase shifter if the following conditions are satisfied: 1) the off-diagonal element of the permeability tensor is negative and its magnitude is not less than the diagonal element, 2) the guide radius is not less than 1.3 times the thickness of the inner conductor, and 3) the phase shift at the cutoff frequencies is not less than π.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the phase characteristics of the ferrite waveguide phase shifter are functions of its structural parameters and of the off-diagonally magnetized ferrites permeability tensor element, which are related to the complex roots of the waveguide characteristic equation and to the real numbers L(c,ρ,n) (c=3DN=1).

The main takeaway from our work is that
the phase shifter operation criteria, established in this paper for the first time, can be used for designing and optimizing such structures.
the phase shifter operation domain, determined by the third criterion, can be extended to higher values of the normalized frequency parameter by increasing the central conductor thickness.

the proposed criteria can be used to determine the optimal parameters of the ferrite waveguide, providing maximum differential phase shift at the required frequency and to predict the behavior of the phase curves in the vicinity of the cut-off frequencies.
